I agree with this. However, I sometimes kind of worry if I have "gaming addiction" right now. I remember a few years ago I was doing a project about video games in my college class. I went to share my assignment with a small group when one of the older college students went "Oh my god I hate video games". I went to ask her why and she said "Because they are so addictive!" I guess she is a parent who worries how much time her kids spend playing video games. She seems very anti gaming. I then had another experience where in my math class during our syllabus one of our teachers turned to the class and said "Oh, and if any of you play video games, DELETE THEM! You are wasting your time!" she then went on to insult people who played video games for a living by saying "Oh, and did you know that there are people who make a living by playing video games?" she seemed really shocked by that response. The next day during break however, she came in the class and showed us a website where I can watch all movies and TV shows online for free. In my head I was thinking: so watching movies and TV shows is fine for her. But video games are seen as a waste of time? This really made me depressed about my hobby. Because I love video games and I have always believed that they do more positive than harm.

Yeah, I do think there is more social stygma to gaming than real harm. I wouldn't say I have ocd but I have slight issues with compulsive behaviours. And I am a perfectionist. I sometimes have a hard time going away from something I am doing before "I feel it's finished". So I had a tendency to spend too much time gaming. But the same happened to while reading a good book, reading/writing on the forums or watching TV. It might seems like an addiction but it isn't as if I can make myself think given task is finished I have no problem to leave games even for few days. Sometimes I don't even feel like gaming. It's just a hobby I extremly enjoy. In fact I think gaming helps me with my compulsions and perfectionism cause while gaming I learn how to let go some things. I play WoW and when achievements were introduced at first I was like "I have to do them all". But then I realized some of them are not in my reach and that I really don't have to do them all at once. Now I'm totally fine with doing them when they happen with no preasure.

There were times when I was ashamed to speak about my hobby. Now I am proud of it. It ain't always easy cause people simply don't understand. But things are changing cause the younger generation is more understanding. I was happy to see some of my friends at work playing some mobile casual games during breaks and even discussing who is on higher level :) Even my mom who used to be like "video games are stupid and I don't like them" started to play mobile games. Tho it took some convincing to make her admitt that those are games as well :D

My family still doesn't totally get why I raid in WoW and why sometimes I'm busy in the evenings. But I guess they in some way accepted it even tho they obviously don't understand it. And yeah it is funny how watching TV or going to a party and getting wasted is more socially accepted. For me watching TV is the biggest brainless waste of time. In fact I used to spend hours in front of TV when I was most depressed cause even gaming seemed like too much effort and only raiding made me get off the couch and make myself to use some thinking. And partying is just not my thing. I didn't like to go to parties even before I had a PC. Since I was a child I enjoyed most to spend time at home. I didn't mind to play with other children but I could find myself entertained on my own quite well.

I think the issue with acceptance towards gaming is similar as why for some reason extraverted behaviour seems to be more accepted than introverted. Tbh I don't really understand why it happens but it does. I mean I don't really understand extraverts but I totally accept them. While I as an introvert don't feel that accepted. Like the fact that I prefer to be alone and limit my human interactions to small group of people makes me an alien or sth ^^

Anyway, to summarize this wall of text. We should stop feeling akward about our hobby I can't let people tell us that it's wrong :) So I might have a hard time to refuse to come to a party because "I have a raid" but then again why should people care for reasons that I don't wanna party and get wasted. I just don't enjoy that and I love my time spent killing big bad bosses in a video game with a bunch of online friends.
